PIA00452.titulo: Solar System Portrait - Earth as Pale Blue Dot
PIA00452.descricao: This narrow-angle color image of the Earth, dubbed Pale Blue Dot, is a part of the first ever 'portrait' of the solar system taken by NASA’s Voyager 1. The spacecraft acquired a total of 60 frames for a mosaic of the solar system from a distance of more than 4 billion miles from Earth and about 32 degrees above the ecliptic. From Voyager's great distance Earth is a mere point of light, less than t

PIA00022.descricao: This photo of Jupiter Great Red Spot was taken by Voyager 1 in early March 1979.

PIA00144.titulo: Jupiter with Satellites Io and Europa
PIA00144.descricao: NASA's Voyager 1 took this photo of Jupiter and two of its satellites Io, left, and Europa on Feb. 13, 1979. Io is above Jupiter Great Red Spot; Europa is above Jupiter clouds. The poles are dark and reddish.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00144

PIA00024.descricao: Saturn and two of its moons, Tethys above and Dione, were photographed by Voyager 1 on November 3, 1980, from 13 million kilometers 8 million miles.

PIA01374.descricao: Both the limb of Saturn and the shadow of its ring system are seen through the transparent C-ring in this striking picture taken by NASA Voyager 1 on Nov. 9, 1980. Gaps and regions of high transparency are seen throughout the C-ring, especially in the a

PIA00359.titulo: Jupiter Great Red Spot and White Ovals
PIA00359.descricao: This photo of Jupiter was taken by NASA Voyager 1 on March 1, 1979. The photo shows Jupiter Great Red Spot upper right and the turbulent region immediately to the west.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00359

PIA18182.titulo: Uranus as seen by NASA Voyager 2
PIA18182.descricao: This is an image of the planet Uranus taken by the spacecraft Voyager 2 in 1986.

PIA00049.titulo: Neptune - Great Dark Spot, Scooter, Dark Spot 2
PIA00049.descricao: This photograph of Neptune was reconstructed from two images taken by NASA Voyager 2. At the north top is the Great Dark Spot.  http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00049

PIA01994.descricao: Intriguing patterns of unknown origin appeared on the surface of Neptune largest satellite, Triton, in this image returned by NASA Voyager 2 on Aug. 22, 1989. Voyager images showed that Triton is one of the brightest objects in the solar system,

ARC-1973-AC73-9253.descricao: Photograph by Pioneer 10   Jupiter at a range of 2584000km (ref: image number sequence A-51 (before) during the 4 days on either side of closest approach) moon seen on upper right on image.

PIA19952.titulo: The Rich Color Variations of Pluto
PIA19952.descricao: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft captured this high-resolution enhanced color view of Pluto on July 14, 2015. The image combines blue, red and infrared images taken by the Ralph/Multispectral Visual Imaging Camera (MVIC). Pluto's surface sports a remarkable range of subtle colors, enhanced in this view to a rainbow of pale blues, yellows, oranges, and deep reds. Many landforms have their own distinc

PIA19968.descricao: NASA's New Horizons captured this high-resolution enhanced color view of Charon just before closest approach on July 14, 2015. The image combines blue, red and infrared images taken by the spacecraft's Ralph/Multispectral Visual Imaging Camera (MVIC); the colors are processed to best highlight the variation of surface properties across Charon. Charon's color palette is not as diverse as Pluto's; m

PIA06193.descricao: While cruising around Saturn in early October 2004, Cassini captured a series of images that have been composed into the largest, most detailed, global natural color view of Saturn and its rings ever made.  This grand mosaic consists of 126 images acquired in a tile-like fashion, covering one end of Saturn's rings to the other and the entire planet in between. The images were taken over the course

PIA14599.descricao: Below a darkened Enceladus, a plume of water ice is backlit in this view of one of Saturn most dramatic moons. This image was captured by NASA Cassini spacecraft.

PIA17172.descricao: On July 19, 2013, in an event celebrated the world over, NASA's Cassini spacecraft slipped into Saturn's shadow and turned to image the planet, seven of its moons, its inner rings -- and, in the background, our home planet, Earth.  With the sun's powerful and potentially damaging rays eclipsed by Saturn itself, Cassini's onboard cameras were able to take advantage of this unique viewing geometry.

PIA21381.descricao: This enhanced-color image of Jupiter's south pole and its swirling atmosphere was created by citizen scientist Roman Tkachenko using data from the JunoCam imager on NASA's Juno spacecraft.  Juno acquired the image, looking directly at the Jovian south pole, on February 2, 2017, at 6:06 a.m. PST (9:06 a.m. EST) from an altitude of about 63,400 miles (102,100 kilometers) above Jupiter's cloud tops.

PIA24681.descricao: This image of the Jovian moon Ganymede was obtained by the JunoCam imager aboard NASA's Juno spacecraft during its June 7, 2021, flyby of the icy moon. At the time of closest approach, Juno was within 645 miles (1,038 kilometers) of its surface – closer to Jupiter's largest moon than any other spacecraft has come in more than two decades.  This image is a preliminary product – Ganymede as seen thr

webb_first_deep_field.descricao: Thousands of galaxies flood this near-infrared image of galaxy cluster SMACS 0723. High-resolution imaging from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope combined with a natural effect known as gravitational lensing made this finely detailed image possible. carina_nebula.titulo: James Webb Space Telescope NIRCam Image of the “Cosmic Cliffs” in Carina Nebula
carina_nebula.descricao: What looks much like craggy mountains on a moonlit evening is actually the edge of a nearby, young, star-forming region NGC 3324 in the Carina Nebula. Captured in infrared light by the Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) on NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope, this image reveals previously obscured areas of star birth.  Called the Cosmic Cliffs, the region is actually the edge of a gigantic, gaseous cavit

sts083-507-023.titulo: Hale Bopp comet seen during STS-83 mission
sts083-507-023.descricao: STS083-507-023 (4-8 April 1997)--- A 35mm camera was used to record this time-exposed image of Comet Hale-Bopp at sunset.  As a spin-off of the more lengthy time exposure, city lights and petroleum fires are seen as distorted streaks.

NHQ202007180001.descricao: The International Space Station, with a crew of five onboard, is seen in this 10 second exposure above comet NEOWISE, Saturday, July 18, 2020 from Keys Gap, W.Va. The comet was discovered by NASA’s Near-Earth Object Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer, or NEOWISE, on March 27. halley_lspn.descricao: O cometa Halley visto da Ilha de Páscoa por W. Liller, da Rede de Fenômenos de Grande Escala do International Halley Watch (NASA).

PIA21747.descricao: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft launched atop its Titan/Centaur-6 launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex in Florida on September 5, 1977, at 8:56 a.m. local time. https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA21747

PIA00030.titulo: Saturn With Rhea and Dione True Color
PIA00030.descricao: NASA Voyager 2 took this true color photograph of Saturn on July 21, 1981. The moons Rhea and Dione appear as blue dots to the south and southeast of Saturn, respectively.

PIA09665.descricao: This five-frame sequence of New Horizons images captures the giant plume from Io Tvashtar volcano. These were snapped by the probe Long Range Reconnaissance Imager LORRI as the spacecraft flew past Jupiter earlier this year.

PIA02321.descricao: This narrow angle image taken NASA Cassini camera system of the Moon is one of the best of a sequence of narrow angle frames taken as the spacecraft passed by the Moon on the way to its closest approach with Earth on August 17, 1999.

PIA02873.descricao: This true-color simulated view of Jupiter is composed of 4 images taken by NASA's Cassini spacecraft on December 7, 2000. PIA21892.descricao: This image of Saturn's northern hemisphere was taken by NASA's Cassini spacecraft on Sept. 13, 2017. It is among the last images Cassini sent back to Earth. The view was taken in visible red light using the Cassini spacecraft wide-angle camera at a distance of 684,000 miles (1.1 million kilometers)

PIA14447.titulo: Earth Triptych from NASA Juno Spacecraft
PIA14447.descricao: This trio of NASA Junocam views of Earth was taken during Juno close flyby on October 9, 2013.

PIA20707.descricao: This color view from NASA's Juno spacecraft is made from some of the first images taken by JunoCam after the spacecraft entered orbit around Jupiter on July 5th (UTC). The view shows that JunoCam survived its first pass through Jupiter's extreme radiation environment, and is ready to collect images

NHQ201808120013.descricao: The United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy rocket launches NASA's Parker Solar Probe to touch the Sun, Sunday, Aug. 12, 2018 from Launch Complex 37 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida. Parker Solar Probe is humanity’s first-ever mission into a part of the Sun’s atmosphere called the corona.

Parker-2024-12-24.titulo: The Closest Images Ever Taken of the Sun's Atmosphere (Parker Solar Probe WISPR)
Parker-2024-12-24.descricao: Image from the WISPR (Wide-Field Imager for Solar Probe) camera captured during Parker Solar Probe's record-breaking closest approach to the Sun on Dec. 24, 2024, showing coronal structures and solar wind streaming out. Released in July 2025.

Pioneer11-Saturn-1979.titulo: Pioneer 11 Image of Saturn and Its Moon Titan
Pioneer11-Saturn-1979.descricao: This image from Pioneer 11 shows Saturn and its moon Titan. The irregularities in ring silhouette and shadow are due to technical anomalies in the preliminary data later corrected. At the time this image was taken, Pioneer was 2,846,000 km (1,768,422 miles) from Saturn.

PIA00111.descricao: This colorized picture of Venus was taken Feb. 14, 1990, from a distance of almost 1.7 million miles, about 6 days after NASA's Galileo made it closest approach to the planet. http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00111

PIA00114.titulo: Earth - South America First Frame of Earth Spin Movie
PIA00114.descricao: This color image of the Earth was obtained by NASA's Galileo at about 6:10 a.m. Pacific Standard Time on Dec. 11, 1990, when the spacecraft was about 1.3 million miles from the planet during the first of two Earth flybys on its way to Jupiter. The color composite used images taken through the red, g

PIA00139.titulo: Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 Fragment W Impact With Jupiter
PIA00139.descricao: These four images of Jupiter and the luminous night-side impact of fragment W of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 were taken NASA's Galileo spacecraft on July 22, 1994. http://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA00139

PIA10176.descricao: As NASA MESSENGER spacecraft drew closer to Mercury for its historic first flyby, the spacecraft Narrow Angle Camera NAC on the Mercury Dual Imaging System MDIS acquired an image mosaic of the sunlit portion of the planet.

GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001920.titulo: First NAC Image Obtained in Mercury Orbit
GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001920.descricao: NASA image acquired: March 29, 2011 This is the first image of Mercury taken from orbit with MESSENGER’s Narrow Angle Camera (NAC). PIA19448.descricao: Today, the MESSENGER spacecraft sent its final image. Originally planned to orbit Mercury for one year, the mission exceeded all expectations, lasting for over four years and acquiring extensive datasets with its seven scientific instruments and radio science investigation. PIA14313.titulo: Latest Image of Vesta captured by Dawn on July 17, 2011
PIA14313.descricao: This is the first image obtained by NASA Dawn spacecraft after successfully entering orbit around Vesta.

PIA19312.descricao: The slim crescent of Ceres smiles back as the dwarf planet awaits the arrival of an emissary from Earth. PIA05571.titulo: Comet Wild 2 Up Close and Personal
PIA05571.descricao: On January 2, 2004 NASA's Stardust spacecraft made a close flyby of comet Wild 2 (pronounced "Vilt-2"). PIA03671.descricao: This image shows the return capsule inside a protective covering. The capsule, which landed at 2:10 a.m. Pacific time 3:10 a.m. Mountain time, contains cometary and interstellar samples gathered by NASA Stardust spacecraft.

PIA02137.descricao: This spectacular image of comet Tempel 1 was taken 67 seconds after it obliterated NASA Deep Impact impactor spacecraft.

PIA13602.descricao: Image taken by NASA EPOXI mission spacecraft during its flyby of comet Hartley 2 on Nov. 4, 2010. The spacecraft came within about 700 kilometers 435 miles of the comet nucleus at the time of closest approach.

OSIRIS-REx-Bennu-arrival.titulo: Bennu PolyCam mosaic obtained at arrival
OSIRIS-REx-Bennu-arrival.descricao: Mosaic of asteroid Bennu made from images taken by the PolyCam imager of NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft on Dec. 2, 2018, from about 24 km, released with the press release "NASA's newly arrived OSIRIS-REx spacecraft already discovers water on asteroid".

OSIRIS-REx-TAG-2020-10-20.descricao: Frame from the SamCam imaging sequence of NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft showing the TAGSAM sampler head touching the surface of asteroid Bennu at the Nightingale site during the Touch-And-Go sample collection on Oct. 20, 2020.

NHQ202309240002.descricao: The sample return capsule from NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission is seen shortly after touching down in the desert, Sunday, Sept. 24, 2023, at the Department of Defense's Utah Test and Training Range. The sample was collected from the asteroid Bennu in October 2020 by NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft. Photo Cre

DART-2022-09-26.titulo: Last image showing all of Dimorphos by DART
DART-2022-09-26.descricao: Last image showing the whole of asteroid Dimorphos, captured by the DRACO camera aboard NASA's DART spacecraft seconds before the kinetic impact on Sept. 26, 2022.

Lucy-Dinkinesh-2023-11-01.descricao: First look at asteroid Dinkinesh and its small companion from the L'LORRI imager aboard NASA's Lucy spacecraft during the Nov. 1, 2023 flyby, which revealed that the satellite (named Selam) is itself a contact binary.

Lucy-Donaldjohanson-2025-04-20.descricao: Image of asteroid Donaldjohanson, a contact-binary-shaped main-belt asteroid, taken by the L'LORRI imager of NASA's Lucy spacecraft near closest approach on April 20, 2025.

NHQ202310130017.descricao: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket with the Psyche spacecraft onboard is launched from Launch Complex 39A, Friday, Oct. 13, 2023, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA’s Psyche spacecraft will travel to a metal-rich asteroid by the same name orbiting the Sun between Mars and Jupiter to study it’

ESA-Juice-2024-08-19.titulo: Juice snaps Moon en route to Earth
ESA-Juice-2024-08-19.descricao: Image of the Moon taken by one of Juice's Monitoring Cameras (JMC) during the lunar-Earth flyby of August 2024. Also visible are parts of the spacecraft and its antennas and booms. ESA/Juice/JMC, licença CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO.

PIA26567.titulo: Europa Clipper Captures Mars, Phobos, and Deimos
PIA26567.descricao: NASA's Europa Clipper captured this infrared image of the heat radiation from Mars and its moons Phobos (closest to Mars) and Deimos (seen in upper left corner) on Feb. 28, 2025, as the spacecraft approached the Red Planet while en route to the Jupiter system to investigate the icy moon Europa. The

ESA-BepiColombo-2021-10-01.descricao: The joint European-Japanese BepiColombo mission captured this view of Mercury on 1 October 2021 as the spacecraft flew past the planet for a gravity assist manoeuvre. Taken at 23:41:12 UTC by the Mercury Transfer Module's Monitoring Camera 2 from 1410 km. ESA/BepiColombo/MTM, licença CC BY-SA 3.0 IG

ESA-BepiColombo-2025-01-08.titulo: Best images from BepiColombo's sixth Mercury flyby
ESA-BepiColombo-2025-01-08.descricao: A selection of the best monitoring-camera images from BepiColombo's sixth and final Mercury flyby on 8 January 2025, when the spacecraft passed 295 km above the surface. ESA/BepiColombo/MTM, licença CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO.

ESA-SolarOrbiter-2022-03-26.descricao: Image of the Sun taken by the Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUI) on Solar Orbiter at perihelion, 27 March 2022, when the spacecraft was about 0.32 AU from the Sun. ESA & NASA/Solar Orbiter/EUI Team, licença CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO.

ESA-SolarOrbiter-2025-03-20.titulo: Solar Orbiter's view of the Sun's south pole
ESA-SolarOrbiter-2025-03-20.descricao: View of the Sun's south pole from the Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUI) on Solar Orbiter, obtained when the spacecraft reached a heliographic latitude of about 17 degrees in March 2025 - the first images of the Sun's poles from outside the ecliptic plane. ESA & NASA/Solar Orbiter/EUI Team, licença CC

art001e000274.titulo: Artemis I flight day 6: A close up of the Moon
art001e000274.descricao: art001e000274 Nov. 21, 2022 -- On the sixth day of the Artemis I mission, Orion's optical navigation camera was commanded to take this black-and-white photo of the lunar surface. Orion uses the optical navigation camera to capture imagery of the Earth and the Moon at different phases and distances,

art001e000673.titulo: Artemis I Flight Day 13: Orion, Earth, and Moon
art001e000673.descricao: art001e000673 (Nov. 28, 2022) On flight day 13, Orion reached its maximum distance from Earth during the Artemis I mission when it was 268,563 miles away from our home planet. Orion has now traveled farther than any other spacecraft built for humans.

art001e002164.descricao: art001e002164 (Dec. 5, 2022): Cameras mounted on the crew module of the Orion spacecraft captured these views of the Moon’s surface. On flight day 20 of the Artemis I mission, the spacecraft made its second and final close approach to the Moon before its returned powered flyby burn.

KSC-20221211-PH-JMB01-0003.descricao: At 12:40 p.m. EST, Dec. 11, 2022, NASA’s Orion spacecraft for the Artemis I mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean with the USS Portland seen in the distance after a 25.5 day mission to the Moon. Orion will be recovered by NASA’s Landing and Recovery team, U.S. Navy and Department of Defense par

ESA-Gaia-DR1-2016-09-14.descricao: All-sky map showing the density of stars observed by Gaia during its first 14 months of observations (July 2014 to September 2015), released with Gaia Data Release 1 on 14 September 2016. Brighter regions indicate denser concentrations of stars. ESA/Gaia/DPAC, licença CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO.

GSFC_20171208_Archive_e002112.descricao: This EIT 171 image shows a wide variety of loops and active regions (lighter areas on the surface). Taken on November 9, 1998. The 171 filter shows emission from 8 and 9 times ionized iron at about 1 million degrees C. Credit: NASA/GSFC/SOHO/ESA To learn more go to the SOHO website: sohowww.nascom.n

ESA-Rosetta-2015-08-13.descricao: Single frame Rosetta navigation camera image acquired at 01:04 GMT on 13 August 2015, just one hour before Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko reached perihelion. Taken around 327 km from the comet, 28 m/pixel, processed to bring out the details of the comet's activity. ESA/Rosetta/NAVCAM, licença CC BY

Hubble-3I-ATLAS-2025-07-21.descricao: Hubble Space Telescope image of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS taken on 21 July 2025, three weeks after its discovery on 1 July 2025. The surrounding streaks are background stars trailed by tracking the comet. NASA, ESA, D. Jewitt (UCLA); Image Processing: J. DePasquale (STScI).
